name: British Gold Coast
alt: Gold Coast Colony and Ashanti and Northern Territories

predecessors.name: Danish Gold Coast
predecessors.text: all Danish forts and settlements, including Christiansborg, Fredensborg, Prinsensten, Kongensten and Augustaborg

predecessors.name: Dutch Gold Coast
predecessors.text: Elmina and the Dutch forts, incorporated on 6 April 1872

successors.name: Ghana
successors.text: the Gold Coast as the pages define it: the Colony, Ashanti and the Northern Territories, i.e.

ledger.x: 1821: the British Gold Coast colony is established, with its capital at Cape Coast.
1850: the Danish forts join the Gold Coast.
6 April 1872: Britain takes over the Dutch Gold Coast.
1873: the Asante invade the new British protectorate.
1874: Lagos is placed under the Gold Coast.
4 February 1874: the British take Kumasi and the war is won.
24 July 1874: the Gold Coast Colony is proclaimed.
24 July 1874: the Gold Coast Colony extends inland.
1877: the colonial capital moves from Cape Coast to Accra (Christiansborg).
1886: Lagos becomes a separate colony again.
January 1896: Ashanti becomes a British protectorate.
1897: the Northern Territories become a British district.
ledger.cp: Mamprusi, Dagarti, Wa and Bona chiefdoms

ledger.x: 1898-1899: the northern frontiers are fixed.
March 1900: the War of the Golden Stool begins.
September 1900: the rising is crushed.
26 September 1901: Ashanti ceases to be a protectorate.

26 September 1901: Ashanti is annexed as a Crown colony under a Chief Commissioner, 'under the Governor of the Gold Coast'; the infobox says the territories 'became part of the Gold Coast colony in 1902', and the Gold Coast page 'In 1902, the British proclaimed Asante a colony under the jurisdiction of the governor of…
27 December 1916: British Togoland is administered with the Gold Coast.
December 1956: British Togoland leaves the Gold Coast's administration and is incorporated.
6 March 1957: the Gold Coast becomes independent as Ghana.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Ashanti War
wars.outcome: British victory in 1874; the Asante were required 'to renounce any claim to many southern territories' and the Gold Coast Colony was proclaimed on 24 July 1874.

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Ashanti War
wars.outcome: Kumasi occupied in January 1896 without fighting; the Asante state became a protectorate (1896 on the Gold Coast page, 1897 on the Anglo-Ashanti wars page).

wars.name: War of the Golden Stool
wars.outcome: Asante rising defeated (infobox March to September 1900); the leaders were exiled to the Seychelles; Ashanti 'classed as a colony by conquest' by the Order in Council of 26 September 1901.

wars.name: Togoland campaign
wars.outcome: The German colony surrendered on 26 August 1914; British forces occupied the west (British Togoland page: 'Occupation: 27 August 1914').

certainty.note: Forts, a coastal protectorate and (from 1896) the Ashanti and northern treaty areas with no surveyed lines on the pages opened; the Fante and Asante frontiers moved by treaty and conquest.
'In 1898 and 1899, European colonial powers amicably demarcated the boundaries between the Northern Territories and the surrounding French and German colonies' (Gold Coast page).
